incidents.title: Stray cattle in Chamarajanagar suffer due to plastic waste menace | Mysuru News - The Times of India
incidents.article_text: Mysuru: Despite a ban on single-use plastics in Chamarajanagar district, 5 cows and 7 goats underwent surgery in the last three months to remove plastic waste from their stomachs. The surgeries, conducted in the district headquarters, highlight the devastating impact of plastic pollution on stray cattle that feed on food in garbage bins.In the last three months, from Jan until the third week of March, veterinarians attached to the govt animal husbandry hospital and polyclinics successfully removed plastic waste, including metal pieces, metal wires, and other sharp objects, from the stomachs of five stray cattle and seven goats. The hospital reports two to four cases every month due to the unscientific disposal of plastic waste.Though the district administration and Chamarajanagar city municipal council put a blanket ban on single-use plastic materials like plastic covers, cups, and plates, people continue to throw leftover food wrapped in plastic covers by the roadside along with garbage, which attracts stray cattle. Sharp objects and polythene bags indiscriminately thrown with waste end up in the belly of these stray animals. Cows and goats fall victim to intestine and stomach disorders. The owners of such animals approach veterinarians at the last stages, seeking treatment after their animals suffer from disorders, tumours, nausea, a decline in milk yield, and swollen bellies from consuming plastic.Speaking to TOI, chief veterinarian at Chamarajanagar district animal husbandry department polyclinic, Dr Murthy said that the hospital has witnessed such cases in recent months, which necessitates raising awareness among the public to save cattle and goats from consuming hazardous plastic waste. Stray cattle consuming plastic can lead to serious health problems, including ruminal impaction, malnutrition, digestive issues, and even death. "Plastic builds up in their stomachs, preventing the animals from properly digesting food. It also results in a decline in milk yield and quality, as the nutritional value of milk depends on what cows are fed. The toxic elements in such cow's milk cannot be removed if they are fed plastic," he said.The cattle were brought in the last stages of treatment for consuming plastic waste, making it difficult to operate on such cases and save lives after surgery, said Dr Murthy. "As cattle and goats fall victim to the indiscriminate disposal of plastic waste, I request the district administration and city civic body to implement tough measures, including banning grazing in the streets of Chamarajanagar, and to step up measures to eliminate the usage of single-use plastic covers and materials," said Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha and Hasiru Sene general secretary Mahesh Prabhu.

incidents.title: Andhra milk contamination: Death toll rises to 13, seven undergoing treatment - News Today | First with the news
incidents.article_text:
The death toll in the suspected milk adulteration incident in East Godavari district has risen to 13, while seven persons continue to receive treatment at hospitals in Rajamahendravaram, an official said on Thursday.

Health department officials said the cluster of cases was first noticed on February 22 after several elderly residents were admitted to hospitals with symptoms such as anuria, vomiting, abdominal pain and acute renal dysfunction requiring dialysis.

Residents from Chowdeswaranagar and Swaroopanagar areas of Lalacheruvu reportedly fell ill after consuming milk suspected to be adulterated and supplied in the locality.

"The death toll in the suspected milk adulteration case in East Godavari district has reached 13, while seven persons are undergoing treatment at hospitals in Rajamahendravaram," the official said.

incidents.title: Toll from adulterated milk in Andhra Pradesh's East Godavari district rises to 6
incidents.article_text:
Toll from adulterated milk in Andhra Pradesh's East Godavari district rises to 6

A six-year-old boy and a 58-year-old woman undergoing treatment died on Tuesday, state health commissioner G Veerapandian said

The toll from alleged consumption of adulterated milk at Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh's East Godavari district has risen to six with the death of two more people, officials said, adding preliminary investigation indicated that leakage of coolant gas in a milk-chilling unit of the private firm led to the contamination.

A six-year-old boy and a 58-year-old woman, undergoing treatment, died on Tuesday morning, state health commissioner G Veerapandian said. He added that at least seven others are said to be in critical condition.

Veerapandian said forensic teams collected milk samples for examination and preliminary assessments suggest that the coolant leakage may have contaminated the milk. He added the exact cause and manner of adulteration would be established after the investigation.

A second official said Varalakshmi Dairy was using ethylene glycol as the coolant at a refrigeration unit, which leaked and contaminated the milk supply, resulting in poisoning among consumers.

"Ethylene glycol is commonly used as a coolant in automobiles and industrial chillers, but not in milk chilling units due to its high toxicity. Instead, food grade propylene glycol is typically used in the dairy and food industries as a safer alternative," the official said.

Veerapandian said the victims had been purchasing milk from the same supplier for nearly a decade. Consumers first began noticing a change in the milk taste. Soon, many complained of vomiting and severe illness, prompting hospitalisations.

"Since all the victims belonged to the same locality, doctors grew suspicious. Patients informed authorities that the illness began after consuming milk. On 16 [February], the supplier delivered milk to 110 families. Blood samples from 315 individuals have been collected and sent for testing. Reports are awaited," Veerapandian said. Addala Ganesh, who ran the diary, was arrested on Monday.

Deputy police superintendent Devakumar, the investigating officer in the case, said the Varalakshmi Dairy has been seized and that it operated without permissions. He added that the investigation was ongoing and further action would be taken based on forensic and medical findings. Devakumar said regulatory lapses and the operation of unauthorised dairy units were being examined.

- ABOUT THE AUTHORSrinivasa Rao Apparasu

Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana . He has over three decades of reporting experience.

incidents.title: FDA food safety drive: 33 held, 27 units sealed
incidents.article_text:
FDA food safety drive: 33 held, 27 units sealed

During the raids, the FDA detected 34 locations involved in the manufacture or sale of banned gutkha, pan masala and tobacco products. The seized material is estimated to be worth around ₹20.48 crore.

Mumbai: Days after taking charge as commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Tukaram Mundhe launched a statewide crackdown on food adulteration, banned products and unhygienic food manufacturing practices. Over the past three days, the FDA arrested 33 people, sealed 27 establishments and seized adulterated and unsafe food products worth crores, officials said on Thursday.

The drive was carried out across multiple divisions in Maharashtra to curb activities affecting public health. Officials said the operation targeted organised adulteration rackets, banned products such as gutkha and tobacco mixtures, counterfeit food products and units violating food safety norms.

The FDA also collected food samples worth approximately ₹28.68 lakh for laboratory analysis. These included drinking water, milk, noodles, carbonated beverages, edible oils, sweet fennel, ice cream, pulses, spices, khoya, paneer, ghee, gram flour and bakery products.

Mundhe said strict legal action would be initiated against those endangering public health. "Those who play with people's health will not be spared. Along with offences under the Food Safety and Standards Act, criminal cases will also be registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023," he said.

Among the major violations detected during the drive were a noodle manufacturing unit in Dharavi found violating food safety regulations, a fake milk racket in Jalgaon, seizure of chemically ripened mangoes worth ₹20 lakh in Pune's Indapur, where ethylene was allegedly used for artificial ripening, and an unhygienic besan manufacturing unit in Dhule district.

incidents.title: Sweet Death: Why Ethylene Glycol, An Antifreeze Chemical, Is Lurking In Andhra's Milk
incidents.article_text:
Sweet Death: Why Ethylene Glycol, An Antifreeze Chemical, Is Lurking In Andhra's Milk

Andhra Pradesh Milk Adulteration Tragedy: What exactly is ethylene glycol, why is it used, and how did it end up in something as routine as milk?

The death toll from the contaminated milk tragedy in Andhra Pradesh's East Godavari has touched 16, triggering alarm across the region. Residents in areas like Lalacheruvu, Chaudeswarnagar and Swaroopnagar began falling ill from mid-February, reporting symptoms such as vomiting, stomach pain and an inability to urinate shortly after consuming milk supplied by a local dairy unit.

Many required dialysis and ventilator support. Laboratory tests later confirmed the presence of a toxic substance — ethylene glycol — in the milk, with doctors linking the deaths to multi-organ failure triggered by acute renal damage.

Recommended Stories

- Brazil Vs Japan Predicted Starting 11 Lineups For FIFA World Cup 2026 Round Of 32 Clash

- NHRC Takes Cognisance Of Lucknow Coaching Centre Fire, Seeks Action Taken Report Within 2 Weeks

- 7 Best Refrigerator Organizer Sets Under ₹1,000

So, what exactly is ethylene glycol, why is it used, and how did it end up in something as routine as milk?

What Is Ethylene Glycol?

Ethylene glycol is a colourless, odourless chemical with a mildly sweet taste, widely used in industrial applications. It is best known as a primary ingredient in anti-freeze and engine coolants because of its ability to lower the freezing point of liquids. While it is useful in controlled environments, it is highly toxic to humans if ingested.

What Are Its Legitimate Uses?

Ethylene glycol has several legitimate industrial applications, including antifreeze and coolants in automobiles, de-icing fluids for aircraft and runways, production of polyester fibres and plastics, hydraulic brake fluids, and industrial solvents.

In all these cases, its use is strictly regulated and never intended for food or consumption.

How Does It Get Linked To Milk Adulteration?

Its presence in milk is both illegal and dangerous, but not entirely inexplicable. Ethylene glycol's sweet taste and thick consistency can make diluted or poor-quality milk appear richer than it is. Unscrupulous suppliers may use it to artificially increase viscosity of the liquid. It also deceptively improves mouthfeel of watered-down milk while masking the inferior quality.

However, unlike more commonly reported adulterants like starch or urea, ethylene glycol is acutely toxic even in small quantities, making its use particularly hazardous.

What It Does To The Human Body

The danger of ethylene glycol lies not just in the chemical itself, but in how the body processes it. Early symptoms that occur within hours are nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and dizziness. These symptoms can resemble routine food poisoning, delaying diagnosis.

Once ingested, the liver metabolises ethylene glycol into harmful compounds such as glycolic acid and oxalic acid. These disrupt the body's acid-base balance and lead to metabolic acidosis, which means dangerously high acidity in the blood.

Next comes kidney failure. Toxic byproducts form crystals in the kidneys and block normal filtration, resulting in acute renal failure, often marked by little or no urine output. This is what has been reported in most cases in Andhra.

If untreated, this kidney failure progresses rapidly, affecting other organs like heart and brain. This in turn can lead to multi-organ failure and death within days.

Why Is It So Difficult To Detect?

The adulteration of ethylene glycol in milk is very difficult to detect without forensic tests because of its colourless and odourless nature. Its sweet taste does not raise suspicion and early symptoms are quite non-specific. Severe damage occurs after a delay, reducing chances of timely intervention.

The Bigger Problem

The Andhra Pradesh incident underscores a worrying shift in food adulteration, from dilution to toxic contamination. The use of an industrial chemical like ethylene glycol points to serious gaps in monitoring and regulation, particularly in local dairy supply chains serving large numbers of households.

Ethylene glycol may be a routine industrial chemical, but in food, it becomes a deadly poison. Its detection in milk is not just adulteration, it is a public health emergency with potentially fatal consequences.

incidents.title: NHRC takes suo motu cognisance of 16 milk adulteration deaths in Rajamahendravaram
incidents.article_text:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Thursday took suo motu cognisance of the milk adulteration case that has claimed 16 lives so far in Rajamahendravaram since February.

According to an official release issued by the NHRC, it also served notices on Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad and Director General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta, seeking a report within two weeks on the health status of the survivors, investigation into the incident, and compensation, if any, offered by the State government to the families of the next of kin of the deceased.

Twenty persons, mostly elderly people and three infants, suffered acute renal failure allegedly after consuming milk supplied by a vendor on February 15 and 16 at various locations in Rajamahendravaram.

"Reportedly, the milk was adulterated with a toxic substance identified as ethylene glycol,which caused multi-organ failure. The suspected source of contamination has been traced to a dairy in Narsapuram village, which was supplying milk to more than 100 households in the area. The Commission has observed that the deaths raise serious issues of human rights violations of the victims," the release stated.

As of March 26, only one victim survived and was discharged from hospital, while three were still battling for life in private hospitals in Rajamahendravaram.

The State government has been offering free medical treatment to the victims and has deployed a team of expert doctors to treat them.

Published - March 26, 2026 08:35 pm IST

incidents.title: 18 yrs on, 4 convicted in adulteration case | Mumbai News - The Times of India
incidents.article_text: Mumbai: In a verdict on a nearly two-decade-old case of milk adulteration, the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate Court in Mumbai convicted four individuals for manufacturing counterfeit milk packets and sentenced them to three years of rigorous imprisonment (RI).Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Vinod R Patil pronounced the judgment last week, convicting Ramlu Guruyayya (65), Yadgiri Gandhashri (63), Yadayya Gattigorla (46), and Suresh Shelar (66). Each convict was also fined Rs 5,000, failing which they will undergo an additional one month of RI.The case dates back to Sept 10, 2006, when then-PSI Shripad Kale got a tip-off of suspicious activities at Khalil Compound, Saki Naka. A police raid led to the arrest of two individuals and the seizure of a large quantity of material, including printing dyes of various milk companies, plastic rolls, fake packaging bags, and printing and cutting machines, all allegedly used to manufacture counterfeit milk packets.You Can Also Check: Mumbai AQI | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Gold Rate Today in Mumbai | Silver Rate Today in MumbaiThe prosecution examined 20 witnesses, including panch witnesses, shop owners, printing service providers, and dairy company officials. The evidence that was submitted revealed a well-organised operation where forged milk packaging was used to mislead customers into believing they were purchasing branded milk."The counterfeit bags bore fake logos and mismatched colour schemes, clearly indicating they were not genuine," observed the court. While the defence, represented by advocates Wahab Khan, RV Gupta, and SR Vani, argued that the accused had been falsely implicated and pointed out inconsistencies in witness testimonies, the court rejected these claims. incidents.title: Rajamahendravaram Milk Contamination Case: Milk contamination case toll rises to five in Rajamahendravaram, accused vendor arrested | Vijayawada News - The Times of India
incidents.article_text:
Rajamahendravaram: The death toll in the acute kidney failure cases reported in Rajahmundry rose to five on Tuesday. A six-year-old boy, Bathina Manohar from the Quarry Market area, who was suffering from anuria, was admitted to KGH in Visakhapatnam and died on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, in connection with cr.No.90/2026 of III Town L\&O Police Station, which was initially registered under Section 194 BNSS and later altered to Sections 103, 105, and 275 BNS, police investigations have uncovered serious lapses related to adulterated milk being sold in the region.

According to the DSP, Kovvur, G Deva Kumar, the accused, Addala Ganeswara Rao alias Ganesh (32), a resident of Narasapuram village in Korukonda mandal, voluntarily appeared before the police on Feb 23. During interrogation in the presence of mediators, he confessed that he had been operating an unauthorized milk collection centre named Varalakshmi Dairy for the past 11 years without any government approval.

According to his statement, glycol from the freezer used to store milk had leaked and contaminated the milk. On Feb 15, he noticed that milk in one can had frozen at the bottom. Despite receiving complaints of bitterness from initial customersâChonga Ramakrishna, Chonga Govindaraju, Peddapati Nageswara Rao and Dengeti Nagendraâhe continued selling the milk.

His brother-in-law, Degala Gangadhara of Narendra Puram, had warned him that the freezer might be defective and glycol leakage could make the milk poisonous, advising him not to sell it. Ignoring this, driven by profit, the accused sold the contaminated milk on February 16 to around 100â105 consumers in Rajamahendravaram and his village.

Many customers later reported bitterness and fell ill, requiring treatment at various hospitals. During the investigation, it was also established that Tadi Krishnaveni of Gandhipuram-4 died on February 22 after consuming the adulterated milk, further increasing the case's severity.

Police have arrested the accused and initiated action to produce him before court for judicial remand and the court remanded him to remand till March 10. Further investigation is underway, focusing on technical evidence and medical reports of the affected victim

incidents.title: AP milk contamination death toll rises to 10, toxic antifreeze presence confirmed
incidents.article_text:
Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.

The contaminated milk that has claimed the lives of 10 people in Andhra Pradesh's Rajahmundry contained ethylene glycol, a toxic antifreeze chemical, forensic tests have confirmed.

East Godavari district Collector Kirthi Chekuri said a report from the Regional Forensic Laboratory in Vijayawada found the presence of ethylene glycol in the milk, according to The Hindu.

Tests were conducted on blood samples of those who died or were hospitalised after consuming milk supplied by Varalakshmi Milk Dairy in Narasapuram village of Korukonda mandal, as well as on the milk samples themselves.

A 72-year-old woman, B Ananthalakshmi, died on March 7, taking the death toll to 10, Eenadu reported. She had been hospitalised since February 17 and was undergoing dialysis after suffering kidney failure, similar to the other victims.

Among the deceased is a six-year-old boy, while three of the victims were in their seventies.

On February 22, the East Godavari District Medical and Health Officer received information from KIMS Hospital about multiple admissions of elderly patients presenting with anuria (absence of urine output), vomiting, abdominal pain and acute renal dysfunction requiring dialysis.

Clinical findings indicated acute renal failure, with elevated blood urea and serum creatinine levels suggesting toxic exposure.

A preliminary epidemiological investigation pointed to milk consumption as the likely source of exposure. Authorities found that milk from Varalakshmi Milk Dairy had been supplied to 106 families. The supply from the dairy was immediately halted.

The milk vendor, Addala Ganeswara Rao, had allegedly distributed the contaminated milk to about 110 customers across Rajahmundry on February 15 and 16.

Police have registered a criminal case and arrested the vendor, who reportedly admitted that he had been operating the dairy without government authorisation for the past 11 years. He also said that ethylene glycol from a freezer used to store the milk had leaked, contaminating the supply.

incidents.title: FDA seize suspected adulterated food items worth ₹ 14.35 lakh
incidents.article_text:
FDA seize suspected adulterated food items worth ₹ 14.35 lakh

FDA Pune seized ₹14.35 lakh worth of suspected adulterated food during the Ganesh Festival, conducting inspections across multiple districts for public safety.

As part of its special drive during the Ganesh Festival, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Pune seized samples of suspected adulterated and substandard food items worth ₹ 14.35 lakh, the officials said.

The drive was conducted in Pune, Solapur, Satara, Sangli and Kolhapur districts. During the special drive Food Business Operators (FBO) and food items were checked for adulteration, hygiene and absolute implementation of food safety norms, the officials said.

"In Pune district, 48 inspections of food establishments were conducted. A total of 53 food samples, including milk, khoya, paneer, mawa, ghee, butter, and namkeen, were collected for analysis. Besides, the FDA seized adulterated ghee, butter, sweet khoya, and vanaspati ghee worth ₹5,16,438," a senior FDA official said.

Suresh Annapure, joint commissioner (Food), FDA, Pune division, said the drive was carried out in the interest of public health and safety for effective implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the regulations of 2011.'

'During the Ganesh festival, the FDA conducted a significant operation in Pune district and region. A total stock worth ₹14,35,958 was seized, including ₹5,16,438 in Pune district and ₹9,19,520 in Pune division,' the FDA said in a statement released on Friday.

Annapure said that samples of the suspected food items are sent to the laboratory for analysis and the reports are awaited.

"The action will be taken as per the provision of the law if the suspected food items are found adulterated, substandard or unsafe for consumption. If required the food licenses of the FBO can be also suspended or cancelled in case of gross violation as per the rules," he added.

Further action will be taken once the analysis reports are available. The FDA has urged citizens to report suspected food adulteration by contacting the Food Administration's toll-free number 1800222365.

incidents.title: NHRC Takes Cognisance of 16 Deaths Due to Adulterated Milk, Seeks Report
incidents.article_text:
NHRC Takes Cognisance of 16 Deaths Due to Adulterated Milk, Seeks Report

Notices sent to officials over adulterated milk deaths in East Godavari

Vijayawada: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has taken suo motu cognisance of the deaths of 16 persons due to the consumption of adulterated milk in East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh in mid-February.

The Commission has issued notices to the Chief Secretary and the Director General of Police, seeking a detailed report within two weeks.

The NHRC said the report should include details of the victims' health condition, the status of the investigation, and compensation, if any, paid to the next of kin.

Taking note of media reports, the Commission observed that if the allegations are found to be true, they would raise serious concerns of human rights violations.

It noted that the affected persons suffered severe health complications, including abdominal pain, vomiting, anuria and acute renal dysfunction, and that most of the victims were elderly persons or young children.

incidents.title: Four dead after consuming 'adulterated' milk in Andhra Pradesh
incidents.article_text:
Four dead after consuming 'adulterated' milk in Andhra Pradesh

The vendor has been detained for questioning.

Four persons have died of acute renal failure after consuming allegedly adulterated milk in Andhra Pradesh's Rajamahendravaram city, The Hindu reported on Monday.

The deaths, including three senior citizens, took place between Saturday and Monday, the newspaper quoted the East Godavari district administration as saying.

At least eight other persons had fallen ill after consuming the milk, the administration was quoted as saying. They are suffering from anuria, or the failure of the kidneys to produce urine, and are undergoing treatment in Rajamahendravaram and Kakinada, The Hindu reported.

Three of them are children below the age of four and are critical, the newspaper quoted doctors as saying.

The symptoms of renal failure began a day after the festival of Maha Shivratri, which was on February 15, The Times of India quoted residents as saying.

District Collector Kirthi Chekuri told The Hindu that the persons had consumed milk supplied by the same vendor, who has been detained for questioning.

The milk had been procured from more than 40 dairy farmers and was being supplied to over 100 families. All persons who died and are ill are from the same area of the city.

Samples have been collected from 75 families, the chief minister's office said.

The samples of the milk and the fodder given to the cattle have been sent for forensic tests.

Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the matter on Monday.

incidents.title: Building a healthy platter⦠| Ranchi News - Times of India
incidents.article_text:
Ranchi: Imagine starting your day with a slice of bread slathered with jam, but a spurious one â a mix of artificial colours and sweeteners, devoid of any real fruit. Or picture sipping on milk that's mostly watered down or laced with chemicals. And for those who love paneer, what if it's not made from milk at all, but something that looks like milk and contains artificial fat and toxic substances?

This is the alarming reality of food adulteration, which has hit Jharkhand hard with recent seizures of thousands of kilograms of spurious milk products and other food items from various locations. This rampant, illegal and dangerous practice not only undermines the nutritional value of our daily food but also poses serious health risks. The sheer scale of adulteration demands stringent action to ensure the food available in the market is safe and wholesome.

Unfortunately, food safety officers (FSOs) have found several adulterated items ranging from milk, and various milk products, including paneer, khowa and ghee to mustard oil, pulses, different kinds of sauces, ice creams, spices and sweets, across the state. Chaturbhuj Meena, the official in charge of the Jharkhand State Food Laboratory, said they have found adulterants in all these food items consumed every day.

"The range of adulterated food items is very vast and lots of food products found in the market both in rural and urban areas are adulterated. While the milk products found in rural areas are free of adulterants, other products are found highly adulterated and vice versa. Adulterated paneer contains arrowroot and other starches. Extensive use of palm oil has been found in the lab and ghee containing artificial fragrances has also been detected," Meena said.

The presence of artificial colour to make it appear like pure mustard oil and artificial fragrance have also been found. "And these oils even in packaged form are blatantly being sold in rural areas as the buyers are not much aware of the products they are buying and do not check the components. Sweets tested in the laboratory have even found artificial dyes used in garment factories. We have not been able to test meat and fish products in large numbers due to some infrastructural issues. However, the tested products are found unadulterated, so far," he added.

Notably, the adulterated food items, especially milk-based products, often come from neighbouring states, while many are also produced in Jharkhand as well.

In recent times, the state health department has been taking many initiatives to maintain a proper check and balance of food items. However, the efforts are often weakened due to various logistical shortcomings and manpower crunches.

Ajoy Kumar Singh, additional chief secretary of health, medical education and family welfare, said the department has directed the FSOs and other designated officers to increase the number of inspections of food service providers like restaurants, hotels, dhabas, sweet shops and take food samples, especially focusing on milk, paneer, khowa, sauce, spices and oil.

"Special drives in districts bordering other states to curb the entry of adulterated food items are also going on. However, the ground officers often find logistical support lacking. Vehicle unavailability is one such issue. Manpower shortage is also another challenge. However, the department is proactively working to curb the menace," Singh said.

He said measures to overcome the challenges were also in process. "At present, JPSC is undertaking the recruitment process of 56 FSOs. The new officers will give a new boost to the department's efforts. Moreover, an MoU with FSSAI is in the pipeline and funds for vehicles will also be provided," Singh added.

A source said though extensive raids were made resulting in the arrest of many who resort to adulteration, the low rate of prosecution and absence of exemplary punishment has been a major roadblock.

"Despite strict legal provisions of imprisonment and levying hefty fines on food adulterators, the slow legal procedures have boosted the confidence of the culprits. FSOs can only conduct raids and seize the products along with the culprits, but only the judiciary can punish them. Many cases are pending in CJM courts across the state," an official added.

incidents.title: Rajahmundry crime: ఆరుకు చేరిన కల్తీపాల మృతులు.. పలువురి ఆరోగ్యం విషమం
incidents.article_text:
ఇప్పటికీ అధికారులకు అందని రిపోర్టులు

Rajahmundry crime: రాజమహేంద్రవరంలో జరిగిన కల్తీ పాలు ఘటనలో మృతుల సంఖ్య పెరిగింది. మృతుల సంఖ్య సోమవారం ఐదు నుండి 6గురికి చేరింది. దీంతో, 20 మంది కల్తీపాల బాధితుల్లో.. మరో 14 మంది ఇంకా ఆస్పత్రిలోనే చికిత్స పొందుతున్నారు. ఈ కల్తీపాల వ్యవహారంలో ప్రభుత్వం సీరియస్ గా ఉండడంతో.. యంత్రాంగం బాధితుల వైద్యం విషయంలో ప్రత్యేక శ్రద్ధ కనబరుస్తున్నారు. వైద్య నిపుణులను రంగంలోకి దించడంతోపాటు, ఆధునిక వైద్య పరికరాలను కూడా ఇక్కడకు రప్పించారు. వారి పర్యవేక్షణలో వైద్య పర్యవేక్షణ కొనసాగిస్తున్నారు. ఏది ఏమైనప్పటికీ వారందరినీ ఆరోగ్య వంతులుగా చేయడానికి తమవంతు ప్రయత్నం చేస్తున్నారు. అయితే ప్రభుత్వ యంత్రాంగం పూర్తిస్థాయిలో వీరికి వైద్య సేవలు ఆరంభించే సమయానికి వాళ్ల పరిస్థితి విషమంగా ఉండడంతో.. కొందరు ఇప్పటికీ కోలుకోవడం లేదు.
